text:
Sara (support): @here Lyra's dedicated cluster is hitting TPS SLO violations again — they're getting 429s and increased latency after the morning burst. Customer reports started at ~08:10 UTC.
Tom (sre): Can you paste the 429 examples and admission_control logs?
Sara (support): pasted below, short sample from their proxy: `429 TOO MANY REQUESTS` and our admission log: `admission:denied account=lyra reason=burst_credits_exhausted pool=dedicated-lyra`
Noah (eng-runtime): Hmm their burst_credits metric looks odd. From metrics: `burst_credits{account="lyra"} 120` at 07:50 then `burst_credits 0` at 08:09 and negative spikes to `-30` at 08:11. That shouldn't happen.
Anya (ml-infra): Negative credits for sure indicates accounting drift between the admission service and accounting worker. Could be a race during concurrent admissions + async accounting ACKs.
Tom (sre): Did we recently deploy anything to admission or accounting?
deploy-bot: deployment rollout: admission-service v3.14 -> v3.15 completed at 2026-01-19T07:58:20Z by noah (canary 10% -> 100%)
Noah (eng-runtime): That rollout did include a minor refactor of the credit decrement path. I pushed a follow-up fix in the PR but it was gated.
Sara (support): Lyra also reported sudden latency spikes ~1200ms p95 for token generation, previously stable ~220ms. They used the burst window for a promotional burst (expected).
Tom (sre): Repro steps requested: 1) send steady baseline at 50 TPS, 2) ramp to 700 TPS sustained for 45s, 3) observe admission decisions and `burst_credits` from /metrics. Run this against their dedicated cluster id `ded-lyra-01`.
Tom (sre): Quick check command I ran on staging: ```bash
wrk -t8 -c100 -d60s https://ded-stg-lyra/api/generate -s ramp.lua --rate 700
# watch metrics: curl http://metrics-host:9090/metrics | grep burst_credits
```
Anya (ml-infra): Also watch KV cache eviction and `kv_cache_ms` — noisy neighbors cause cache churn and add latency even before admission fires.
Noah (eng-runtime): I'm going to roll the accounting worker patch to canary on ded-lyra-01 and leave admission v3.15 pinned for 5m to see if drift stabilizes.
Maria (billing): FYI if burst credits went negative, the billing system currently has a guard that prevents charging for negative balances, but the customer-facing dashboard shows 0 and that confuses customers. We should avoid transient negatives.
Sara (support): I told Lyra we'll throttle gracefully and open a case update once we have root cause.
Tom (sre): Forensics checklist: 1) pull admission logs 07:45-08:30 UTC, 2) accounting worker ack logs same window, 3) trace incoming request ids and correlate with admission decisions, 4) cpu/mem on accounting worker (we saw GC spikes last week).
Noah (eng-runtime): Patch rolling to canary now. I expect metric correction within 2-3 minutes after accounting reconcilier runs. Will post back.
obs-bot: Alert suppressed: tps-slo-violation (lyra) — ticket #INC-2026-712 created
Tom (sre): If canary doesn't fix it, fallback plan: switch Lyra to burst-policy conservative mode (lower per-request credit draw) and enable temporary additional dedicated headroom (spin up an extra GPU node) while we fix accounting.
Sara (support): Sounds good. I'll update the customer: explain we've got a targeted canary and a fallback plan.
Noah (eng-runtime): Canary shows credits stabilizing: `burst_credits` back to 95 -> 110 and no more negatives. Latency p95 dropping to ~260ms. I'll let it run 10m then promote.
Maria (billing): I'll add a note to the billing dashboard team to hide transient negatives and show a tooltip.
Sara (support): Thanks everyone — I'll post the customer update and close the loop after promotion. :thumbsup:
Noah (eng-runtime): Promoting patch to prod at 08:25 UTC.
Tom (sre): Closing investigative loop checklist in the ticket. Leave thread for any follow-ups.
